citation: A. Dubietis, G. Jonusauskas, A. Piskarskas, "Powerful femtosecond pulse generation by chirped and stretched pulse parametric amplification in BBO crystal", Opt. Commun. 88(4-6), 437-440 (1992)
readMethod: macOS PDFKit text layer (4 pages) plus page images at 1.8x; figures 2 and 3 were read off the images (shapes only). The PDF and figures are not in the repository.
topic: OPCPA: fibre-chirped 1.055 um pulses amplified by 2e4 in BBO, compressed to 70 fs

referenceNumbers.value: Nd:glass oscillator, 1.7 ps (Gaussian assumed), 27 cm^-1 wide, 1.055 um
8 um core, 4.5 m; chirped over 155 cm^-1 (steepness ~30 cm^-1/ps), ~5 ps; ~8 nJ; linear chirp up to 9 GW/cm^2 input intensity = 4.5 kW peak
8 ps pump gave the most efficient amplification of the 5 ps chirped pulse; 3 mJ at 527.5 nm (SH in 2 cm KDP, from 11 mJ); stretcher range 2.8-15 ps
BBO, 8 mm, type I, beams crossed ~2 deg, pump waist 0.3 mm diameter (f = 1 m lens), signal = fibre core imaged by a 16x objective; gain bandwidth up to 400 cm^-1 at 1.055 um
600 lines/mm reflection grating, pair of flat mirrors, near Littrow, single-pass grating-pair equivalent; optimum length 170 mm
70 fs (sech^2; autocorrelation FWHM 110 fs), predicted 67 fs, time-bandwidth 0.325, efficiency ~64 %, 65 uJ, 0.9 GW, compression ratio ~24

assumptions: Seed for the OPA and compressor: a sech^2 pulse whose spectrum is 155 cm^-1 wide (transform limit 67.8 fs, which is the paper's 'predicted 67 fs'), with a linear chirp of 30 cm^-1/ps (GDD 1.77e5 fs^2, 5.17 ps). This is the paper's own description of the chirped pulse; the fibre stage is simulated separately (A) and disagrees with it.
Fibre: FusedSilica dispersion (the doped core is not given), n2 = 2.6e-20 m^2/W, A_eff = 4.5 kW / 9 GW/cm^2 = 50 um^2 (derived from the paper), scalar field.
'Crossed at ~2 deg' is taken as the angle inside the crystal; beams: signal radius 64 um, pump radius 150 um; the 1-D Gaussian-overlap crystal model.
The pump energy at the crystal is not given. Only the 3 mJ of second harmonic is. The pump energy that gives 100 uJ of signal in the engine is reported as an inferred quantity.
The compressor's incidence angle is 'near Littrow' (18.45 deg at 1055 nm); 170 mm is read as the perpendicular separation of the equivalent single-pass pair (the folded layout is not specified).
Idler compression, beam ellipticity from the lateral walk-off of a single-pass compressor, spatial effects in the OPA and the 1.7 ps -> 27 cm^-1 oscillator pulse shape are not modelled.
